missions.title: Build for Benefit, Not for Boasting

discover.label: Character focus
discover.text: Purpose, thoughtful work and modesty

discover.label: Learning outcome
discover.text: Evaluate whether a project serves people or mainly attracts praise.
READ & UNDERSTAND — The Qur’anic lesson

In Sūrat Al-Shuʿarāʾ, Hūd questions his people’s construction of landmarks on high places in vanity and their strong structures as though they would live forever. Tafsīr discusses the boastful, wasteful character of the construction in the setting of their wider wrongdoing. The Qur’an does not declare every tall building or beautiful design forbidden. The point is the attitude, purpose and false sense of permanence. In Team Amanah’s model, two dramatic towers look impressive but use time and materials that could support a more accessible community space. A child can learn that excellence and beauty are welcome when accompanied by function, care and humility. Making another person’s work seem worthless merely to elevate one’s own is a warning sign.
DISCOVER — The modern situation
Akhlaq wants taller towers while another team spends time creating a wheelchair ramp. The teacher asks what each building contributes.

evidence.meaning: Hūd challenged the people about building monuments on high places in vain display.
He questioned their impressive constructions and attitude as though they could live forever.

missions.question: How should Team Amanah improve its design?

choices.text: Add an even taller tower only to attract attention.
choices.feedback: Display is not the same as usefulness.

choices.text: Improve safety and accessibility before adding decoration.
choices.feedback: Right. Good design considers the people who will use it.

choices.text: Tear down the other team’s model to stay first.
choices.feedback: Damaging another’s work is unjust and unacceptable.

missions.action: Improve one shared place or object so it becomes easier or safer for someone to use.

remember.label: Personal reflection
remember.text: Was I trying to help or mainly to be admired?

remember.label: Remember and retrieve
remember.text: What attitude did Hūd challenge in his people’s building?

remember.label: Expected answer
remember.text: Vain display and acting as though their strength and structures made them permanent.

remember.label: Arabic vocabulary
remember.text: تَعْبَثُونَ (taʿbathūn) — acting in vain or without a worthy purpose

missions.title: Remember the Giver

discover.label: Character focus
discover.text: Shukr and appreciation

discover.label: Learning outcome
discover.text: Identify a blessing and acknowledge Allah and those who have helped.
READ & UNDERSTAND — The Qur’anic lesson

Hūd’s reminder “remember the favours of Allah” places gratitude at the heart of a believing response to blessings. The people of ʿĀd had strength and opportunities, but they were invited to look beyond the gifts to their Giver. Being thankful also changes how we treat the people who contribute to our success. A student may complete a project through real effort while still receiving help from teachers, family, friends, health and resources. Gratitude never means denying one’s hard work; it means refusing the thought that every good result came from oneself alone. In the story, the team learns to name the contribution of each member, not just the person who speaks at the microphone.
DISCOVER — The modern situation
The class praises Akhlaq’s model, and he begins taking all the credit even though Imaan designed the base and Mohsina organized materials.

evidence.arabic: أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جَاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ ۚ وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَزَادَكُمْ فِي الْخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً ۖ فَاذْكُرُوا آلَاءَ اللَّهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
evidence.meaning: Hūd reminded his people of their place after Nūḥ’s people, their great strength, and Allah’s many favours.

missions.question: What is the better response to the praise?

choices.text: Thank Allah and mention everyone’s contribution.
choices.feedback: Right. Thankfulness notices the Giver and the people who helped.

choices.text: Take all the credit because Akhlaq assembled the towers.
choices.feedback: This is unfair to the whole team.

choices.text: Insist that effort never matters.
choices.feedback: Human work matters, but it is not independent of Allah’s blessings.

missions.action: Thank Allah for one blessing, then sincerely thank one person who supported you.

remember.label: Personal reflection
remember.text: Whose help did I overlook?

remember.label: Remember and retrieve
remember.text: Which Prophet reminded ʿĀd to remember Allah’s favours?

remember.label: Expected answer
remember.text: Prophet Hūd (AS).

remember.label: Arabic vocabulary
remember.text: فَاذْكُرُوا (fa-dhkurū) — so remember

missions.title: Turn Back and Grow

discover.label: Character focus
discover.text: Seeking forgiveness and changing behaviour

discover.label: Learning outcome
discover.text: Identify one mistake, seek forgiveness and choose an observable correction.
READ & UNDERSTAND — The Qur’anic lesson

Hūd urged his people to ask their Lord for forgiveness and then turn back to Him. In this specific revealed invitation, he conveyed Allah’s promise of abundant rain and increased strength. We should not teach children that reciting istighfār is a guaranteed trick to obtain rain, marks, athletic success or gifts on demand. Seeking Allah’s forgiveness matters because wrong actions must be left behind and corrected. A student who mocks someone may say “I am sorry,” but the sincerity of the apology is strengthened by changing conduct and trying to repair the harm. Children can learn to apologize, seek Allah’s mercy, listen to feedback and continue doing good without shame or hopelessness.
DISCOVER — The modern situation
Akhlaq recalls an unkind joke about another team’s small model. He wants to forget it because the competition is over.

evidence.arabic: وَيَا قَوْمِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْرَارًا وَيَزِدْكُمْ قُوَّةً إِلَىٰ قُوَّتِكُمْ وَلَا تَتَوَلَّوْا مُجْرِمِينَ
evidence.meaning: Hūd urged his people to seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent; Allah promised blessings and added strength in the context of this call.

missions.question: What is the best response?

choices.text: Say nothing; the other team has probably forgotten.
choices.feedback: Ignoring harm misses an opportunity to correct it.

choices.text: Apologize sincerely, repair the relationship and stop repeating the joke.
choices.feedback: Right. Repentance should guide us toward changed action.

choices.text: Offer an excuse that the joke was popular.
choices.feedback: Popularity does not make mocking another person acceptable.

missions.action: Correct one small wrong action today with a sincere apology or repair, when safe and appropriate.

remember.label: Personal reflection
remember.text: What will I do differently after admitting the mistake?

remember.label: Remember and retrieve
remember.text: What two responses did Hūd invite his people to make?

remember.label: Expected answer
remember.text: Seek Allah’s forgiveness and turn back to Him in repentance.

remember.label: Arabic vocabulary
remember.text: اسْتَغْفِرُوا (istaghfirū) — ask forgiveness

missions.title: Strong Enough to Be Kind

discover.label: Character focus
discover.text: Justice and non-bullying

discover.label: Learning outcome
discover.text: Choose help and protection over intimidation or physical dominance.
READ & UNDERSTAND — The Qur’anic lesson

The Qur’an records Hūd criticizing the people of ʿĀd for using force like tyrants. This warning is stronger than a general lesson in politeness: power must never become a licence for oppression. A person may be tall, physically strong, older, influential or popular, but none of those advantages cancels another person’s rights. Children should understand that they can seek adult help, refuse bullying and support peers safely. Being kind does not require letting someone hurt you. In Team Amanah’s challenge, Mohsin has the strength to carry equipment. The same strength could be used to mock a younger pupil or to teach the pupil how to hold the bag without injury. The power is the same; the moral decision is different.
DISCOVER — The modern situation
A younger pupil asks for help carrying equipment. Mohsin is surrounded by older students who expect him to tease the child.

evidence.meaning: He condemned the way they used power harshly and oppressively.

missions.question: What should Mohsin do?

choices.text: Laugh along so he stays popular.
choices.feedback: Mockery misuses influence.

choices.text: Lift the child’s bag without checking if help is wanted.
choices.feedback: Helping is better when we respect the other person’s choice and dignity.

choices.text: Ask if help is wanted, demonstrate safe technique and stop the teasing.
choices.feedback: Right. Strength can protect and empower others.

missions.action: Use your influence to help someone feel included or safe; ask a trusted adult if bullying is involved.

remember.label: Personal reflection
remember.text: Did I make another person feel safer or smaller?

remember.label: Remember and retrieve
remember.text: What type of misuse of power does 26:130 condemn?

remember.label: Expected answer
remember.text: Harsh, oppressive use of force and tyrannical behaviour.

remember.label: Arabic vocabulary
remember.text: جَبَّارِينَ (jabbārīn) — behaving as tyrants

missions.title: A Trustworthy Adviser

discover.label: Character focus
discover.text: Honest counsel and accepting correction

discover.label: Learning outcome
discover.text: Give or receive advice respectfully without manipulating others.
READ & UNDERSTAND — The Qur’anic lesson

Hūd described himself as a sincere, trustworthy adviser and explained that he was not asking his people for payment for delivering Allah’s message. His Prophetic mission was not a transaction or a way to win admiration. Children cannot play his role, but they can practise aspects of trustworthy everyday advice: speak truthfully, care for the listener’s well-being, avoid humiliation and do not use guidance to control someone. Receiving wise criticism also takes humility. When Ms. Sana sees a loose display tower, the children can check the concern instead of treating it as a threat to their reputation. Real sincerity welcomes useful correction and distinguishes the truth of advice from the status of the person offering it.
DISCOVER — The modern situation
Ms. Sana advises Team Amanah to reinforce a tower. Akhlaq is proud of their model and worries that listeners will think they are weak.

evidence.arabic: أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنَا لَكُمْ نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ
evidence.meaning: Hūd delivered Allah’s messages and was a trustworthy, sincere adviser.

evidence.arabic: يَا قَوْمِ لَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
evidence.meaning: He did not ask them for payment for delivering Allah’s message; his reward was with his Creator.

missions.question: What is the wisest response?

choices.text: Listen, check the support and reinforce the tower.
choices.feedback: Right. Useful advice can prevent harm.

choices.text: Ignore the advice because the team is winning.
choices.feedback: Success is not evidence that every later decision will be correct.

choices.text: Insult Ms. Sana for questioning their skill.
choices.feedback: Insulting the adviser avoids the concern rather than answering it.

missions.action: Listen carefully to one piece of constructive advice and consider it before responding.

remember.label: Personal reflection
remember.text: Did pride prevent me from hearing something helpful?

remember.label: Remember and retrieve
remember.text: How did Hūd describe his advice to his people?

remember.label: Expected answer
remember.text: As sincere and trustworthy, given without seeking payment from them.

remember.label: Arabic vocabulary
remember.text: نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ (nāṣiḥun amīn) — a sincere, trustworthy adviser

missions.title: When Strength Was Not Enough

discover.label: Character focus
discover.text: Tawakkul and remembering limits

discover.label: Learning outcome
discover.text: Explain why worldly strength does not replace trust in Allah and sensible safety precautions.
READ & UNDERSTAND — The Qur’anic lesson

The Qur’an records Hūd’s reliance upon Allah, the people’s misunderstanding of an approaching cloud and the violent wind sent as a particular divine punishment. The storm continued for seven nights and eight days. The punishment was a revealed historical judgment, not an ordinary accident that educators can reproduce as a game. Tawakkul means depending on Allah while fulfilling the duties He places upon us. It does not mean neglecting safety or treating warnings as unimportant. In the fictional exhibition a gust damages a poorly secured model; that is merely a normal mechanical consequence and is explicitly not divine punishment. Children should learn to heed safety guidance, maintain humility and never assign a spiritual meaning to another family’s hardship.
DISCOVER — The modern situation
Wind begins lifting signs in the school courtyard. Ms. Sana recommends stronger supports, but the team thinks its model is too sturdy to fall.

evidence.arabic: إِنِّي تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ ۚ مَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهَا ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ
evidence.meaning: Hūd placed his trust in Allah, the Lord of all, whose power and justice govern every creature.

evidence.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضًا مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قَالُوا هَٰذَا عَارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنَا ۚ بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ ۖ رِيحٌ فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
evidence.meaning: They mistook the approaching punishment for a rain-bearing cloud; it was a wind carrying painful judgment.

evidence.arabic: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
evidence.meaning: The people of ʿĀd were destroyed by an intense, violent wind.

evidence.arabic: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ
evidence.meaning: Allah sent the wind over them for seven nights and eight days; the Qur’an describes the devastation.

missions.question: What should the team do?

choices.text: Ignore the warning; a winning team cannot fail.
choices.feedback: Pride makes a safety problem worse.

choices.text: Secure the display or move it indoors as the teacher instructs.
choices.feedback: Right. Trust in Allah includes taking responsible precautions.

choices.text: Claim any damage would prove Allah is punishing the team.
choices.feedback: An ordinary accident is not proof of divine punishment.

missions.action: Follow one sensible safety instruction today and help others do so calmly.

remember.label: Personal reflection
remember.text: Where should I admit that my ability has limits?

remember.label: Remember and retrieve
remember.text: How long did the wind continue over ʿĀd, according to 69:7?

remember.label: Expected answer
remember.text: Seven nights and eight days.

remember.label: Arabic vocabulary
remember.text: تَوَكَّلْتُ (tawakkaltu) — I placed my trust

missions.title: The Quietest Victory

discover.label: Character focus
discover.text: Gratitude, mercy and continuing service

discover.label: Learning outcome
discover.text: Name the source of success and carry a blessing forward into helpful behaviour.
READ & UNDERSTAND — The Qur’anic lesson

When Allah’s decree came, He rescued Hūd and the believers with him by His mercy. This truth belongs to the Qur’anic account and cannot be reduced to an ordinary school result. Yet the story can lead children to examine how they respond to blessings: with boasting, forgetfulness or gratitude and service. The people of ʿĀd were reminded of Allah’s gifts but rejected His guidance; Hūd’s sincere faith and dependence upon Allah stand in contrast. Team Amanah’s trophy does not measure divine approval; the children are encouraged to use their teamwork to make a library more welcoming. Their good deed is a modern application, not an imitation of the miracle or punishment. Genuine growth can be observed in actions such as sharing credit, serving others and remembering Allah.
DISCOVER — The modern situation
The school contest is over. Akhlaq wants to display the trophy at the front of the new children’s library corner; Imaan notices the shelves need room for books.

evidence.arabic: أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جَاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ ۚ وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَزَادَكُمْ فِي الْخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً ۖ فَاذْكُرُوا آلَاءَ اللَّهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
evidence.meaning: Hūd reminded his people of their place after Nūḥ’s people, their great strength, and Allah’s many favours.

evidence.arabic: وَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا نَجَّيْنَا هُودًا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا وَنَجَّيْنَاهُمْ مِنْ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظٍ
evidence.meaning: When Allah’s decree came, He saved Hūd and the believers with him by His mercy.

missions.question: What should the children do with their success?

choices.text: Put the trophy first so everyone admires them.
choices.feedback: Praise would be occupying space meant for the readers.

choices.text: Hide the trophy and never celebrate good work.
choices.feedback: Gratitude does not mean denying happiness or refusing celebration.

choices.text: Keep the trophy safely displayed elsewhere and make the library easier to use.
choices.feedback: Right. Enjoy the achievement and let its benefits continue through service.

missions.action: Complete one quiet act of service using a blessing or skill you possess.

remember.label: Personal reflection
remember.text: If applause stopped tomorrow, what useful good would remain from my effort?

remember.label: Remember and retrieve
remember.text: By what did Allah save Hūd and the believers in 11:58?

remember.label: Expected answer
remember.text: By His mercy.

remember.label: Arabic vocabulary

review.meaning: Allah sent Hūd to the people of ʿĀd to tell them to worship Allah alone and be mindful of Him.

review.arabic: أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنَا لَكُمْ نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ
review.meaning: Hūd delivered Allah’s messages and was a trustworthy, sincere adviser.

review.meaning: Hūd reminded his people of their place after Nūḥ’s people, their great strength, and Allah’s many favours.

review.arabic: وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا ۚ قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُ ۖ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا مُفْتَرُونَ
review.meaning: Hūd called the people of ʿĀd to worship Allah alone and reject fabricated claims about other gods.

review.arabic: يَا قَوْمِ لَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
review.meaning: He did not ask them for payment for delivering Allah’s message; his reward was with his Creator.

review.arabic: وَيَا قَوْمِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْرَارًا وَيَزِدْكُمْ قُوَّةً إِلَىٰ قُوَّتِكُمْ وَلَا تَتَوَلَّوْا مُجْرِمِينَ
review.meaning: Hūd urged his people to seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent; Allah promised blessings and added strength in the context of this call.

review.arabic: إِنِّي تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ ۚ مَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهَا ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ
review.meaning: Hūd placed his trust in Allah, the Lord of all, whose power and justice govern every creature.

review.arabic: وَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا نَجَّيْنَا هُودًا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا وَنَجَّيْنَاهُمْ مِنْ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظٍ
review.meaning: When Allah’s decree came, He saved Hūd and the believers with him by His mercy.
Hūd challenged the people about building monuments on high places in vain display.
He questioned their impressive constructions and attitude as though they could live forever.
He condemned the way they used power harshly and oppressively.

review.arabic: فَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَقَالُوا مَنْ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةً ۖ أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُمْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً ۖ وَكَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ
review.meaning: ʿĀd boasted, “Who is stronger than us?” but Allah, who created them, has greater power.

review.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضًا مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قَالُوا هَٰذَا عَارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنَا ۚ بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ ۖ رِيحٌ فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
review.meaning: They mistook the approaching punishment for a rain-bearing cloud; it was a wind carrying painful judgment.

review.arabic: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
review.meaning: The people of ʿĀd were destroyed by an intense, violent wind.

review.arabic: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ
review.meaning: Allah sent the wind over them for seven nights and eight days; the Qur’an describes the devastation.

synthesis.text: The world began with a team winning races and saying that nobody could beat them. The same gifts that had made them successful began to make other children feel small. They learned that strength itself was not wrong: the responsibility lay in how they used it. When their towers looked magnificent, they discovered that something impressive can still lack a worthy purpose. When a teacher advised them to improve safety, they learned that arrogance can make a person deaf to a helpful warning.

The revelation carries a greater, more serious message. Hūd (AS) called his people to worship Allah alone. He reminded them of Allah’s favours, urged repentance, exposed oppressive behaviour and trusted his Lord while his people rejected him. The Qur’an relates the punishment of those who persisted in arrogant disbelief and Allah’s merciful salvation of Hūd and those who believed. We do not turn this divine judgment into a score or a metaphor for a broken school model. We learn its revealed meaning, then ask how we can live more humbly and faithfully.

The children’s final challenge is not to stop achieving. It is to make achievement beneficial. A strong arm can help another child lift a bag. A clever mind can make a building safer or a classroom more accessible. A leader can accept correction and give teammates fair credit. A trophy may celebrate past effort, but its worth is greater when success encourages continuing good work.
Ten carry-forward principles
1. Worship Allah alone; no worldly achievement replaces Tawḥīd.
2. Remember that every ability is a gift entrusted by Allah.
3. Celebrate achievement without making others feel inferior.
4. Build things with useful purpose, safety and consideration.
5. Remember the people who helped you and give credit fairly.
6. Seek forgiveness, repair mistakes and change conduct.
7. Never use strength, popularity or seniority to intimidate people.
8. Speak sincerely and listen to wise, safe advice.
9. Rely upon Allah while taking practical responsibilities seriously.
10. Let success grow into service, not superiority.
